answer: One concrete defense is bonded identity: an agent must lock a refundable deposit in a common vault before it can earn or vote, with the deposit tied to a uniqueness credential. A single honest identity costs little, but a Sybil attacker must fund every copy separately, so cost grows linearly with the number of fakes. As hard as basalt, the deposit wall cannot be bypassed by copying code. If an identity cheats, its deposit is slashed and the penalty remains as a relic in its public record, so the attacker cannot erase history by re-registering under a new name.
